# Browser profile reconciliation decisions

This is the architect's implementation direction for a PRIVATE candidate, not a released engine capability. Original 20118/d1db… and strict f819… remain historical, unchanged inputs. New canonical contracts/profile/digest must include the reconciled equations and fully expanded containers before live pairing.

Accept the four Core amendment groups and Artist's additional explicit base-0 texture/store-generation rule. Preserve all fifteen resource ceilings, all C0/v3 schemas, twelve Expected fields and nineteen persisted Bindings. Only the new browser family has engine-owned/API-logical release semantics; physical browser/driver/GC reclamation stays UNMEASURED.

Reservations have immutable declared bounds, an unfulfilled/fulfilled union, one actual receiver and a positive owner-held atomic fulfillment receipt. Actual receiver full capacity remains charged. A new artwork acquisition cannot be baseline-visible; baseline is actual constructor inventory only. No reservation discount by returned DTO, SHA equality or a fake release receipt. Unknown fulfillment/release retains debt.

Recursively enumerate browser material, geometry, candidate, trace, range, release, recovery and capacity/source stamp types. Homogeneous receipt domains and complete per-view ownership closure are required. Returning one atlas range releases that range/residency after positive owner verification; it never releases the full shared CPU/API stores or another view. Context end releases API stores only. IDs remain unique across retained owner lifetimes. Texture levels initially form the base-0 contiguous chain; fixed layout/store generation and observed content revision distinguish sub-image updates from storage replacement.

Budget reconciliation: preserve ONE cumulative <=1,000,000 normalized reference-work allowance per authoring attempt, plus the ten independent raw domains in aa73328. Raw counters are never blindly added or exchanged. An explicit immutable backend/rate/coverage table defines normalized reference charges; counters already covered by a backend's normalized charge are not charged a second time. This is a declared cost policy, not a measured CPU-time or RAM bound.

The initial table must use existing semantics: Core actual Budget.take/node/text/hash/copy/output charges contribute their actual reference-unit delta; Artist's actual PreparationWork take/bytes contributes its actual local delta (bytes uses cumulative ceil(bytes/64), already including decoder/copy/upload work sent through workBytes); raw decoder ticks remain independently bounded and are not added again when covered by that same actual Artist byte-work hook. Actual Host/history/codec observers charge their actual visits/text/UTF-8/copy/hash/serialization using the explicitly frozen existing reference rates. No new exchange rate may be invented to fit a fixture. Public repair counters remain separately unbound/zero for the appearance-only route; combined geometry is not authorized. Every coverage row must identify actual source hooks and every uncovered call refuses.

Thus aa73328's ten-domain utility remains useful. The new browser composition adds the one normalized policy/ceiling as a separate owner-enforced gate with source-backed coverage, not a sum of unrelated raw counters. Each domain still has its own fixed tightening-only cap. Work, JSON input/output flows, peak complete WAL/history envelopes and persistent resource stocks remain different quantities. No phase resets, fresh nested allowances or returned-work DTO refunds. A conservative bound may be consumed in full only when explicitly reported as conservative charged work, never mislabeled observed actual work; otherwise missing intrinsic settlement terminates with unresolved reservation.

Begin the actual authoring attempt from the opaque existing source owner before its actual source/history preparation; bind verified source once after paid observation. Hold cleanup/continuation escrow before acquisitions. Permit only the same real ticket at original ordinal+1 and the same operation's actual pending WAL; no Expected restamp. Warm unknown retains the original attempt/resources and freezes writes. Cold outcome-recovery uses a new explicitly recovery-only scope and reconciles the original persisted ID before native acquisition; it cannot finance command replay or resurrect a saved capability. Known-commit presentation retry has its own non-authoring purpose.

Pre-command palette acquisition is a separately bounded resource-owner scope, not an authoring request or editing allowance. It allocates no request/op IDs and grants no editing credit. Actual session.prepare later creates its one authoring attempt and charges its own actual adoption/borrow/copy/validation. The selected builtin prefix remains synchronous, validated and nonempty; the retained exact-artwork/resource/byte-lease route has no prefix. No all-thirty library seed.

First user milestone remains a selected original stamp/detail on a clean current rectangle: explicit content.import if absent, surface.layers and decoration.add in one canonical command, one actual candidate/admission/final bind, one real ticket/WAL, Review and Apply. Then actual update/remove/layers, repeated edits, history, save/reopen/portable parity and unknown/cold recovery. An opacity-only control, grammar fixture or diagnostic pixels are component evidence only. If the actual path exceeds its bounds, optimize the actual paired path or refuse; do not raise bounds or substitute synthetic ready states.

Accuracy: keep distinct observed quantities and real ownership semantics. Efficiency: explicit bounded costs and shared ranges are code-based policy/estimates until measured. Narrative: preserve precise local marks and familiar undo/history behavior. Prefer this browser-specific observable profile for authoring while preserving strict compatibility and its stronger unbound requirements.
